findings.title: canManage() grants manage access to admins holding only the view scope
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the fallback evaluation is `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e. it returns true when the caller has only the 'view' scope on the all-groups resource. An admin granted a view-all-groups permission (but not manage) would therefore pass `requireManage()` and be allowed to create top-level groups via GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup, and any other code path relying on groups().canManage(). The scope list should only contain MANAGE.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns authorization resource IDs instead of group IDs
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds `groupResource.getId()` to the returned set. The returned set is consumed by UsersResource/BruteForceUsersResource as `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute and passed to `session.users().getUsersCount(realm, ..., groupIds)`, where the values must be group IDs used to filter users by group membership. In the V2 schema the group ID is stored as the resource *name* (AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup returns group.getId() as the resource name), while resource.getId() is the internal UUID of the authorization resource. As a result, admins who should see users through group view-members/manage-members permissions will get empty user lists and zero counts because the membership filter uses non-existent group IDs. It should add `groupResource.getName()`.

findings.title: findByType("Groups") matches no per-group resources because V2 resources are created without a type
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. However, per-group V2 resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource(), which never calls `resource.setType(resourceType)` (unlike the V1 GroupPermissions.initialize() that sets type "Group", and unlike the all-resource entries created in init() where the type is set from the ResourceRepresentation). So per-group resources have a null type and findByType("Groups") will only ever return the single all-groups resource — individual group view-members/manage-members permissions are never discovered, breaking user listing for group-scoped admins. Either set the type when creating resources in getOrCreateResource, or look resources up differently.

findings.title: Possible null resource passed to policyStore.findByResource when all-groups resource is missing
findings.body: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(), when no per-group resource exists, `resource` is set to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`, which returns null when the 'Groups' all-resource has not been created (e.g. the admin-permissions client was initialized before this schema version, or the resource was deleted). The very next statement calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` with that possibly-null resource, and after that `new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)` would NPE as well. The same pattern exists in UserPermissionsV2, but this new code repeats it; it should null-check the type resource before using it.
